questions.sec: Extrinsic Allergic Alveolitis: Type IV over III Pathogenesis, Absent Type I Features, and the Twelve-Disease Etiology Table
questions.q: Which synonym and host line open hypersensitivity pneumonitis on page 257?
opts: AKA extrinsic allergic alveolitis, occurring usually in smokers
AKA extrinsic allergic alveolitis, occurring usually in non smokers
AKA intrinsic allergic alveolitis, occurring usually in non smokers
AKA extrinsic allergic bronchiolitis, occurring usually in non smokers
questions.exp: The head of the chapter reads 'AKA extrinsic allergic alveolitis' and 'usually in non smokers' — a useful counterweight to the smoking-associated cystic and interstitial diseases of pages 236–240. (Book p257)

questions.sec: Extrinsic Allergic Alveolitis: Type IV over III Pathogenesis, Absent Type I Features, and the Twelve-Disease Etiology Table
questions.q: Which pathogenesis chain is printed for HP on page 257?
opts: Repeated organic dust inhalation causes hypersensitivity of Type III greater than IV, producing predominantly neutrophilic inflammation of terminal airways, alveoli and interstitium
Single organic dust inhalation causes hypersensitivity of Type IV greater than III, producing predominantly lymphocytic inflammation of large airways only
Repeated inorganic dust inhalation causes hypersensitivity of Type I greater than III, producing predominantly eosinophilic inflammation of terminal airways, alveoli and interstitium
Repeated organic dust inhalation causes hypersensitivity of Type IV greater than III, producing predominantly lymphocytic inflammation of terminal airways, alveoli and interstitium
questions.exp: The chain reads 'Repeated organic dust inhalation → Hypersensitivity (Type IV > III) → Inflammation (Predominantly lymphocytic) of terminal airways, alveoli & interstitium'. Repetition, the IV-over-III order and the lymphocyte all matter. (Book p257)

questions.sec: Extrinsic Allergic Alveolitis: Type IV over III Pathogenesis, Absent Type I Features, and the Twelve-Disease Etiology Table
questions.q: Because there is no type 1 hypersensitivity in HP, which three absences does the pathology block print?
opts: No lymphocytosis, no raised IgE and no diffuse infiltrates
No eosinophilia, no raised IgE and no granulomas
No eosinophilia, no raised IgE and no migratory lung infiltrates
No eosinophilia, no precipitins and no migratory lung infiltrates
questions.exp: The block reads 'No type 1 hypersensitivity → No: Eosinophilia, ↑ IgE, migratory lung infiltrates' — precisely the type 1 triad that Loeffler syndrome displayed on page 250. (Book p257)

questions.sec: Extrinsic Allergic Alveolitis: Type IV over III Pathogenesis, Absent Type I Features, and the Twelve-Disease Etiology Table
questions.q: Which infiltrate evolution and granuloma statement complete the pathology on page 257?
opts: Pulmonary infiltrates are diffuse initially and become a reticulo-nodular pattern, and non caseating granulomas are present
Pulmonary infiltrates are peripheral initially and become diffuse, and non caseating granulomas are present
Pulmonary infiltrates are migratory initially and become reticular, and caseating granulomas are present
Pulmonary infiltrates are diffuse initially and become a reticulo-nodular pattern, and granulomas are absent
questions.exp: The bullets read 'Pulmonary infiltrates: Diffuse (Initially) → Reticulo-nodular pattern' and 'Non caseating granulomas present', the same evolution the CXR line repeats on page 259. (Book p257)

questions.sec: Extrinsic Allergic Alveolitis: Type IV over III Pathogenesis, Absent Type I Features, and the Twelve-Disease Etiology Table
questions.q: Match each thermophilic-actinomycete Disease in the etiology table with its printed source — 1) Farmer's lung, marked most common 2) Bagassosis, marked second most common 3) Mushroom worker's lung … A) Moldy compost or mushroom B) Moldy hay C) Moldy sugarcane
questions.exp: Farmer's lung (m/c) comes from moldy hay, bagassosis (2nd m/c) from moldy sugarcane and mushroom worker's lung from moldy compost/mushroom, all three sharing the merged antigen cell 'Thermophilic actinomycete: Thermoactinomyces vulgaris (m/c antigen)'. (Book p257)

questions.sec: Extrinsic Allergic Alveolitis: Type IV over III Pathogenesis, Absent Type I Features, and the Twelve-Disease Etiology Table
questions.q: Which antigen cell is shared by the next four rows of the etiology table, and which sources accompany them?
opts: Aspergillus clavatus covers compost lung (compost), tobacco worker's lung (barley), malt worker's lung (mold on tobacco) and cheese washer's lung, whose source cell is blank
Aspergillus fumigatus covers compost lung (compost), tobacco worker's lung (mold on tobacco), malt worker's lung (barley) and cheese washer's lung
Thermoactinomyces vulgaris covers compost lung, tobacco worker's lung, malt worker's lung and cheese washer's lung from cheese washings
Aspergillus clavatus covers compost lung (compost), tobacco worker's lung (mold on tobacco), malt worker's lung (barley) and cheese washer's lung, whose source cell is blank
questions.exp: The second merged antigen cell, 'Aspergillus clavatus', spans compost lung, tobacco worker's lung, malt worker's lung and cheese washer's lung, with sources compost, mold on tobacco and barley printed for the first three and the cheese washer source left blank. (Book p257)

questions.sec: Extrinsic Allergic Alveolitis: Type IV over III Pathogenesis, Absent Type I Features, and the Twelve-Disease Etiology Table
questions.q: Match each remaining etiology-table Disease with its printed source and antigen pairing — 1) Hot tub, humidifier or air conditioner lung 2) Bird fancier's lung 3) Wood trimmer's lung 4) Familial HP and chemical worker's lung … A) Source pigeon, parrot or chicken with avian droppings as antigen B) Familial HP from wood pulp with Bacillus subtilis, and chemical worker's lung from polyurethane foams (isocyanate) with its antigen cell blank C) Source cell blank with Cladosporium and MAC as antigens D) Source cell blank with Rhizopus as antigen
questions.exp: Hot tub/humidifier/air conditioner lung pairs a blank source with Cladosporium and MAC; bird fancier's lung pairs pigeon/parrot/chicken with avian droppings; wood trimmer's lung pairs a blank source with Rhizopus; familial HP pairs wood pulp with Bacillus subtilis; and chemical worker's lung prints polyurethane foams (isocyanate) with a blank antigen cell. (Book p257)

questions.sec: Extrinsic Allergic Alveolitis: Type IV over III Pathogenesis, Absent Type I Features, and the Twelve-Disease Etiology Table
questions.q: A non-smoking pigeon keeper develops lymphocytic alveolitis with non caseating granulomas, no eosinophilia and a normal IgE. Which Disease, source and antigen does the page 257 table assign him?
opts: Mushroom worker's lung — moldy compost source, Thermoactinomyces antigen
Bird fancier's lung — pigeon source, avian droppings antigen
Farmer's lung — moldy hay source, Thermoactinomyces vulgaris antigen
Bird fancier's lung — pigeon source, Aspergillus clavatus antigen
questions.exp: Bird fancier's lung is the only row sourced to 'Pigeon/ parrot/ chicken' with antigen 'Avian droppings', and the absent eosinophilia and IgE rise are the no-type-1 signature printed above the table. (Book p257)

questions.sec: Extrinsic Allergic Alveolitis: Type IV over III Pathogenesis, Absent Type I Features, and the Twelve-Disease Etiology Table
questions.q: TRUE or FALSE about the superlatives printed inside the etiology table.
opts: False — bagassosis is marked most common and farmer's lung second most common
False — Aspergillus clavatus is marked the most common antigen
True — bird fancier's lung is marked most common because its row is printed in red
True — farmer's lung is marked the most common Disease and Thermoactinomyces vulgaris the most common antigen, while bagassosis is marked second most common
questions.exp: The table tags 'Farmer's lung (m/c)', 'Bagassosis (2nd m/c)' and, in the merged cell, 'Thermoactinomyces vulgaris (m/c antigen)'. Bird fancier's lung is highlighted in red ink but carries no frequency tag. (Book p257)

questions.sec: Acute, Subacute and Chronic Presentations, Complications, Non-Caseating Granuloma and Emphysema Notes, Precipitins and BAL CD8/CD4
questions.q: Match each HP presentation tempo on page 258 with its printed fate — 1) Acute 2) Subacute 3) Chronic … A) Marked most common B) Can cause fibrosis, that is ILD C) Self resolving
questions.exp: Presentation reads 'Acute: Self resolving', 'Subacute: m/c' and 'Chronic: Can cause fibrosis (ILD)', returning HP to the ILD classification of page 236 in its chronic form. (Book p258)

questions.sec: Acute, Subacute and Chronic Presentations, Complications, Non-Caseating Granuloma and Emphysema Notes, Precipitins and BAL CD8/CD4
questions.q: Which clinical features and timescale define the acute form of HP?
opts: Gradually progressive dyspnea and cough, resolving in 2–4 days
Fever, chills and cough with a raised IgE, resolving in 2–4 weeks
Fever, chills and cough with a raised ESR, resolving in 2–4 days
Fever, chills and cough with a raised ESR, resolving in 2–4 hours as printed
questions.exp: The acute form reads 'Fever, chills, cough (↑ ESR)' with 'Resolves in 2–4 days' beneath it. The raised marker is ESR, not the IgE that type 1 disease would raise. (Book p258)

questions.sec: Acute, Subacute and Chronic Presentations, Complications, Non-Caseating Granuloma and Emphysema Notes, Precipitins and BAL CD8/CD4
questions.q: Which three statements define the subacute form of HP?
opts: Gradually progressive dyspnea and cough with fatiguability, no systemic features, and diffuse involvement without lobar preference as printed
Gradually progressive dyspnea and cough with fatiguability, no systemic features, and upper lobe involvement
Gradually progressive dyspnea and cough with fatiguability, prominent systemic features, and lower lobe involvement
Abrupt dyspnea and cough with fever and chills, and upper lobe involvement
questions.exp: The subacute form reads 'Gradually progressive dyspnea & cough + fatiguability', 'No systemic features' and 'Upper lobe involvement' — the lobar preference that placed HP in the upper-lobe lists on pages 242 and 255. (Book p258)

questions.sec: Acute, Subacute and Chronic Presentations, Complications, Non-Caseating Granuloma and Emphysema Notes, Precipitins and BAL CD8/CD4
questions.q: Match each named HP Disease with its printed complication on page 258 — 1) Bird fancier's lung 2) Farmer's lung … A) Emphysematous changes B) Rarely causes fibrosis or ILD
questions.exp: Complications read 'Bird fancier's lung: Rarely cause fibrosis/ ILD' and 'Farmer's lung: Emphysematous changes'. The commonest HP thus ends in emphysema rather than the fibrosis the chronic form threatens. (Book p258)

questions.sec: Acute, Subacute and Chronic Presentations, Complications, Non-Caseating Granuloma and Emphysema Notes, Precipitins and BAL CD8/CD4
questions.q: Which seven causes of non caseating granulomas are listed in the page 258 Note?
opts: HP, 30% of TB as printed, lymphoma, sarcoidosis, cat scratch disease, Crohn's disease and berylliosis
Sarcoidosis, 30% of TB as printed, lymphoma, cat scratch disease, Crohn's disease, berylliosis and ABPA
HP, 30% of TB as printed, lymphoma, sarcoidosis, cat scratch disease, Crohn's disease and silicosis
HP, TB without any percentage, lymphoma, sarcoidosis, cat scratch disease, ulcerative colitis and berylliosis
questions.exp: The Note lists HP itself, '30 % TB', lymphoma, sarcoidosis, cat scratch disease, Crohn's disease and berylliosis — berylliosis having been introduced as the sarcoid mimic on pages 228–229. HP heads its own granuloma list. (Book p258)

questions.sec: Acute, Subacute and Chronic Presentations, Complications, Non-Caseating Granuloma and Emphysema Notes, Precipitins and BAL CD8/CD4
questions.q: Pick the ODD ONE OUT — three of these are printed on page 258 as diseases causing emphysematous changes apart from COPD, one is not:
opts: Cryptogenic organising pneumonia
Coal worker's pneumoconiosis, marked rare
Bird fancier's lung
Farmer's lung
questions.exp: The second Note lists farmer's lung, cryptogenic organising pneumonia and coal worker's pneumoconiosis (rare) as non-COPD emphysema causes. Bird fancier's lung, in the complications block above, rarely causes fibrosis instead. (Book p258)

questions.sec: Acute, Subacute and Chronic Presentations, Complications, Non-Caseating Granuloma and Emphysema Notes, Precipitins and BAL CD8/CD4
questions.q: What does the Management section print about serum precipitin in HP?
opts: It is always negative because HP has no type III component
It is specific and diagnostic, arising due to type I hypersensitivity
It can be positive but is non-specific, arising due to type IV hypersensitivity
It can be positive but is non-specific, arising due to type III hypersensitivity
questions.exp: Investigations read 'S. precipitin: Can be positive (Non specific): D/t type III hypersensitivity' — the junior partner in the Type IV > III mechanism leaving a serological trace that cannot confirm the diagnosis. (Book p258)

questions.sec: Acute, Subacute and Chronic Presentations, Complications, Non-Caseating Granuloma and Emphysema Notes, Precipitins and BAL CD8/CD4
questions.q: BAL in HP shows lymphocytosis with the printed fraction CD8/CD4 greater than ______.
questions.exp: The BAL line reads 'Lymphocytosis: CD 8 / CD 4 > 2', a CD8-dominant lavage. The inverted ratio for sarcoidosis is given as a mirror note on the next page. (Book p258)

questions.sec: Acute, Subacute and Chronic Presentations, Complications, Non-Caseating Granuloma and Emphysema Notes, Precipitins and BAL CD8/CD4
questions.q: Four days after shovelling moldy hay a farmer's fever, chills and cough with raised ESR settle on their own, but over the following seasons he develops emphysematous change rather than fibrosis. Which tempo and which complication has he shown, in the page's terms?
opts: The subacute form of bird fancier's lung, which rarely causes fibrosis
The acute self-resolving form of farmer's lung, whose printed complication is emphysematous change
The chronic form of farmer's lung, whose printed complication is fibrosis in every case
The acute form of bagassosis, whose printed complication is emphysematous change
questions.exp: Fever, chills, cough and raised ESR resolving in 2–4 days is the acute form, moldy hay makes it farmer's lung, and farmer's lung alone carries 'Emphysematous changes' as its complication on this page. (Book p258)

questions.sec: PFT, CXR and CT in HP with the Head Cheese Pattern, Steroid Response versus Irreversible Fibrosis, and the HP versus ABPA Difference Table
questions.q: Which PFT and CXR statements open page 259, and what captions the chest film?
opts: The PFT is restrictive in acute HP; CXR moves from diffuse opacities to reticulonodular shadows; and the film is captioned 'mosaic tiles attenuation'
In chronic ILD/fibrosis the PFT is obstructive; CXR moves from diffuse opacities to reticulonodular shadows; and the film is captioned 'CXR infiltrates in acute HP'
In chronic ILD/fibrosis the PFT is restrictive; CXR moves from diffuse opacities to reticulonodular shadows; and the film, labelled A, is captioned 'CXR infiltrates in acute HP'
In chronic ILD/fibrosis the PFT is restrictive; CXR moves from reticulonodular shadows to diffuse opacities; and the film is captioned 'CXR infiltrates in chronic HP'
questions.exp: The page opens 'PFT: In chronic form (ILD/ fibrosis): Restrictive pattern' and 'CXR: Diffuse opacities → Reticulonodular shadows', with film A captioned 'CXR infiltrates in acute HP' — the evolution already stated in the pathology on page 257. (Book p259)

questions.sec: PFT, CXR and CT in HP with the Head Cheese Pattern, Steroid Response versus Irreversible Fibrosis, and the HP versus ABPA Difference Table
questions.q: Which three CT findings are printed for HP on page 259?
opts: Centrilobular nodules, bilateral ground glass opacities, and mosaic attenuation or head cheese pattern of varying densities on the same CT
Centrilobular nodules, unilateral ground glass opacities, and honeycombing
Centrilobular nodules, bilateral consolidations, and mosaic attenuation or head cheese pattern of uniform density
Perilobular nodules, bilateral ground glass opacities, and crazy pavement pattern
questions.exp: CT lists 'Centrilobular nodules', 'B/L ground glass opacities (GGO)' and 'mosaic attenuation/ Head cheese pattern (varying densities on same CT)'. Mosaic attenuation was the HP row of the HRCT table on page 241. (Book p259)

questions.sec: PFT, CXR and CT in HP with the Head Cheese Pattern, Steroid Response versus Irreversible Fibrosis, and the HP versus ABPA Difference Table
questions.q: Match each CT image on page 259 with its printed label and caption — 1) Left scan marked B with red arrows 2) Right scan … A) Captioned mosaic tiles attenuation B) Nodular opacity arrows, captioned bilateral GGO and nodular opacity, the pair jointly captioned CT in HP
questions.exp: Scan B carries 'Nodular opacity' arrows over the caption 'B/L GGO & nodular opacity', the right scan is captioned 'mosaic tiles attenuation', and both together are labelled 'CT: HP'. (Book p259)

questions.sec: PFT, CXR and CT in HP with the Head Cheese Pattern, Steroid Response versus Irreversible Fibrosis, and the HP versus ABPA Difference Table
questions.q: Which mirror-image BAL Note is printed for sarcoidosis on page 259?
opts: BAL lymphocytosis with CD4/CD8 greater than 2 indicates sarcoidosis — the inverse of HP's CD8/CD4 dominance
BAL eosinophilia above 40% indicates sarcoidosis
BAL lymphocytosis with CD4/CD8 less than 1 indicates sarcoidosis
BAL lymphocytosis with CD8/CD4 greater than 2 indicates sarcoidosis, identical to HP
questions.exp: The Note reads 'BAL lymphocytosis with CD 4 / CD 8 > 2: Sarcoidosis', deliberately inverting the CD8/CD4 > 2 of HP on page 258 so the two granulomatous diseases separate on lavage. (Book p259)

questions.sec: PFT, CXR and CT in HP with the Head Cheese Pattern, Steroid Response versus Irreversible Fibrosis, and the HP versus ABPA Difference Table
questions.q: Which two treatment statements are printed for HP on page 259?
opts: The subacute form responds to antifungals, but once fibrosis is present the Disease is irreversible
The acute form requires steroids, and fibrosis reverses with prolonged therapy
The subacute form responds to steroids, but once fibrosis is present the Disease is irreversible
All forms respond to steroids including established fibrosis
questions.exp: Treatment reads 'Subacute form: Respond to steroids' and 'If fibrosis (+): Irreversible' — placing the therapeutic window in the most common, subacute, presentation before chronic fibrosis supervenes. (Book p259)

questions.sec: PFT, CXR and CT in HP with the Head Cheese Pattern, Steroid Response versus Irreversible Fibrosis, and the HP versus ABPA Difference Table
questions.q: Match each row of the HP versus ABPA table with its printed pair — 1) Pathology 2) Radiographic features 3) Skin test reaction 4) Blood markers … A) ABPA migratory infiltrates with bronchiectatic changes versus HP diffuse infiltrates becoming reticulonodular opacities B) ABPA positive to A. fumigatus versus HP positive to A. clavatus C) ABPA eosinophilia positive, IgG precipitins positive and serum IgE markedly raised versus HP eosinophilia negative, precipitins positive and serum IgE normal D) ABPA airway colonisation with eosinophilic inflammation and hypersensitivity I plus III versus HP non caseating granulomas with lymphocytic inflammation and hypersensitivity IV over III
questions.exp: Pathology contrasts colonisation and eosinophilic (I + III) inflammation in ABPA with granulomas and lymphocytic (IV > III) inflammation in HP; radiology contrasts migratory bronchiectatic change with diffuse-to-reticulonodular infiltrates; skin tests are positive to fumigatus in ABPA and clavatus in HP; and blood work separates only on eosinophilia and IgE, since IgG Aspergillus precipitins of type III hypersensitivity are positive in both. (Book p259)

questions.sec: PFT, CXR and CT in HP with the Head Cheese Pattern, Steroid Response versus Irreversible Fibrosis, and the HP versus ABPA Difference Table
questions.q: Two patients are skin-test positive to an Aspergillus species with positive IgG precipitins. One has eosinophilia, a markedly raised IgE and migratory infiltrates with bronchiectasis; the other has no eosinophilia, a normal IgE and reticulonodular opacities. Using the page 259 table, name each.
opts: The first is HP reacting to A. clavatus; the second is ABPA reacting to A. fumigatus
The first is ABPA reacting to A. fumigatus; the second is HP reacting to A. clavatus
Both are ABPA, separated only by Disease stage
The first is ABPA reacting to A. clavatus; the second is HP reacting to A. fumigatus
questions.exp: Shared precipitins cannot separate them, but eosinophilia with ↑↑ IgE and migratory bronchiectatic infiltrates fill the ABPA column (fumigatus), while absent eosinophilia, normal IgE and reticulonodular opacities fill the HP column (clavatus). (Book p259)

questions.sec: PFT, CXR and CT in HP with the Head Cheese Pattern, Steroid Response versus Irreversible Fibrosis, and the HP versus ABPA Difference Table
questions.q: TRUE or FALSE about the shared row of the HP versus ABPA table.
opts: True — peripheral eosinophilia is also printed positive in both diseases
False — serum IgE, not precipitins, is the shared positive row
True — IgG Aspergillus precipitins, labelled type III hypersensitivity, are the one test printed positive in both diseases
False — precipitins are positive in ABPA but negative in HP
questions.exp: The row 'IgG Aspergillus precipitins (Type III hypersensitivity)' reads '+ve' under both ABPA and HP, reflecting the type III component each mechanism carries; eosinophilia and IgE split the columns instead. (Book p259)

questions.sec: PFT, CXR and CT in HP with the Head Cheese Pattern, Steroid Response versus Irreversible Fibrosis, and the HP versus ABPA Difference Table
questions.q: The varying densities coexisting on one HP CT are given the alternative name of the ______ pattern.
opts: head cheese
tree in bud
reverse halo
crazy pavement
questions.exp: The CT bullet reads 'mosaic attenuation/ Head cheese pattern (varying densities on same CT)'. Crazy pavement belonged to silicosis and PAP on page 225, and reverse halo to COP on page 240. (Book p259)

units.title: Extrinsic Allergic Alveolitis: Type IV over III Pathogenesis, Absent Type I Features, and the Twelve-Disease Etiology Table
units.sec: Extrinsic Allergic Alveolitis: Type IV over III Pathogenesis, Absent Type I Features, and the Twelve-Disease Etiology Table
units.guide:
HP (p257), AKA extrinsic allergic alveolitis and usually a disease of non-smokers, follows repeated organic dust inhalation through Type IV > III hypersensitivity into lymphocytic inflammation of terminal airways, alveoli and interstitium.
Without type 1 hypersensitivity there is no eosinophilia, no raised IgE and no migratory infiltrates; infiltrates run diffuse then reticulo-nodular, with non caseating granulomas.
The etiology table ranks farmer's lung (most common, moldy hay), bagassosis (second, moldy sugarcane) and mushroom worker's lung under Thermoactinomyces vulgaris (most common antigen); compost, tobacco worker's, malt worker's and cheese washer's lung under Aspergillus clavatus; hot tub/humidifier lung under Cladosporium and MAC; bird fancier's lung under avian droppings; wood trimmer's under Rhizopus; familial HP under Bacillus subtilis from wood pulp; and chemical worker's lung to polyurethane isocyanate, with the table's blank source and antigen cells preserved.

units.title: Acute, Subacute and Chronic Presentations, Complications, Non-Caseating Granuloma and Emphysema Notes, Precipitins and BAL CD8/CD4
units.sec: Acute, Subacute and Chronic Presentations, Complications, Non-Caseating Granuloma and Emphysema Notes, Precipitins and BAL CD8/CD4
units.guide:
Acute HP (p258) is self-resolving fever, chills and cough with raised ESR settling in 2–4 days; subacute HP is the most common tempo, with gradually progressive dyspnea, cough and fatiguability, no systemic features and upper lobe involvement; chronic HP can fibrose into ILD.
Bird fancier's lung rarely fibroses while farmer's lung turns emphysematous, and the notes list non-caseating granulomas in HP, 30% of TB as printed, lymphoma, sarcoidosis, cat scratch disease, Crohn's disease and berylliosis, and non-COPD emphysema in farmer's lung, COP and rarely coal worker's pneumoconiosis.
Serum precipitins may be positive non-specifically through the type III component, and BAL shows lymphocytosis with CD8/CD4 above 2.

units.title: PFT, CXR and CT in HP with the Head Cheese Pattern, Steroid Response versus Irreversible Fibrosis, and the HP versus ABPA Difference Table
units.sec: PFT, CXR and CT in HP with the Head Cheese Pattern, Steroid Response versus Irreversible Fibrosis, and the HP versus ABPA Difference Table
units.guide:
Chronic HP restricts on PFT (p259), the CXR evolves from diffuse opacities to reticulonodular shadows ('CXR infiltrates in acute HP'), and CT shows centrilobular nodules, bilateral GGO and mosaic or head-cheese attenuation of varying densities, captioned as bilateral GGO with nodular opacity and mosaic tiles in HP.
Sarcoidosis mirrors the lavage with CD4/CD8 above 2, subacute HP responds to steroids, and established fibrosis is irreversible.
Against ABPA, HP shows granulomatous lymphocytic (IV > III) pathology, reticulonodular radiology, clavatus skin positivity, no eosinophilia and normal IgE, sharing only the type III IgG precipitins — ABPA instead colonises airways eosinophilically (I + III) with migratory bronchiectatic infiltrates, fumigatus positivity, eosinophilia and markedly raised IgE.
